key_insight: AlB₁₂–Al detonation coatings improved the wear resistance of steel 45, with AB70 showing stable friction and wear behavior across the tested conditions.
engineering_relevance: These coatings offer a potential wear-protection option for steel components exposed to sliding contact.
method: Deposited AB70 (70 wt.% AlB₁₂, 30 wt.% Al) and AB30 (30 wt.% AlB₁₂, 70 wt.% Al) using a DNEPR-5M detonation-spray system.
Characterized coating thickness, hardness, and surface structure.
Evaluated friction and wear under varying sliding speeds and loads.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports coating thicknesses of approximately 170–200 μm, AB70 friction coefficients of 0.21–0.38, and AB70 wear rates of 3.3–8.6 μm/km, with coated samples outperforming uncoated steel 45 in wear resistance.
watch_item: Oxidative and adhesive-abrasive wear depended on sliding conditions, but the abstract does not specify the tested speed and load ranges needed to judge application suitability.
paper_title: Structure and properties of AlB12-Al detonation coatings on steel 45
